paper_metadata.title: A quantum neural network with built-in self-attention mechanism

summary: This paper proposes a variational QNN-SAM model using only parameterized quantum circuits for three benchmark tasks: meteorological forecasting, binary text classification, and stock-price prediction. Reported results include 99.87% / 93.51% / 92.54% accuracy on the meteorological tasks, 100% on MC and 74.19% on RP for text classification, and R2 values up to 0.958 on stock prediction, all using 8-qubit circuits with gate depths around 96 and no named hardware platform.

experiments.description: QNN-SAMo and QNN-SAMb evaluated on meteorological indicator forecasting (atmospheric pressure, temperature, relative humidity) using a parameterized quantum circuit self-attention model.

algorithm.variant: QNN-SAMo / QNN-SAMb (quantum neural network with built-in self-attention)
algorithm.ansatz: U1, U2, U3 parameterized quantum circuits; U2 uses controlled phase gates and Rx-Rz rotation gates; U3 uses CRX-based two-qubit blocks
algorithm.parameter_initialization: random initialization of parameters (five repetitions with random initialization)

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Numerical differencing/normalized values encoded with a single Rx rotation gate for each input value; query, key, and value quantum states are prepared by the encoding circuit
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize mean squared error between predicted and true meteorological indicator values

problem_instance.description: Forecast the fifth day value from the preceding four days for three meteorological indicators
problem_instance.dataset_name: China Meteorological Data Service Center dataset

dataset_specification.description: Three sequences of 800 training and 200 test points; values over consecutive days; preprocessed by differencing and normalization; three previous differencing points used to predict the fourth

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Differencing and normalization; alignment process uses three previous differencing data points to predict the fourth
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Five repetitions with random initialization; prediction accuracy reported as mean ± standard deviation

implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Prediction accuracy computed from relative error; mean squared error used for training

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: Loss curves shown; QNN-SAMo converges faster than QNN-SAMb

speedup_claims.caveats: No asymptotic or empirical speedup claim is made; the paper reports improved accuracy and reduced parameter count versus SAM/QSAM.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: 8 qubits, 96 gate depth, 72 two-qubit gates; no hardware execution reported
limiting_factors: No QPU hardware or runtime evidence
Classical SAM baseline is competitive and sometimes slightly better on some metrics
No asymptotic complexity or crossover analysis
Data loading and variational training overhead dominate

notes: Hardware is not explicitly specified; no QPU or simulator platform named, so hardware.type remains not_specified.

Qubit counts and gate depths are reported in Table 7 for the meteorological tasks, but the paper does not give a single fixed depth for all ansatz variants; values vary by sequence length and architecture.
No asymptotic quantum speedup is claimed; the paper focuses on empirical performance and resource scaling.
The paper reports strong predictive accuracy, but this is a benchmark comparison rather than a demonstrated quantum advantage.
Classical SAM achieves 99.86% / 92.15% / 92.16% on atmospheric pressure / temperature / relative humidity, while QNN-SAMo reaches 99.87% / 93.51% / 92.54%.

experiments.description: QNN-SAMo and QNN-SAMb evaluated on binary text classification tasks (MC and RP) using quantum word embedding and self-attention circuits.

algorithm.ansatz: U1, U2, U3 parameterized quantum circuits; U2 uses controlled phase gates and Rx-Rz rotation gates; U3 uses CRX-based two-qubit blocks
algorithm.parameter_initialization: random initialization of parameters (five repetitions with random initialization)

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Word vectors are embedded using parameterized encoding circuits to obtain query, key, and value quantum states; n1=2 for each word embedding circuit

problem_instance.description: Binary text classification on MC (food vs IT) and RP (subject relative clause vs object relative clause) datasets
problem_instance.dataset_name: MC synthetic dataset; RP synthetic dataset

dataset_specification.description: MC: 17-word vocabulary, 70/30/30 split; RP: 115-word vocabulary, 74/31 split, with 52 train-only words, 19 test-only words, 46 shared words

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Words represented by word vectors (pre-trained embeddings implied); encoding circuits used for word embedding; no additional preprocessing beyond embedding described
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Reported accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score; results shown for MC and RP; five repetitions with random initialization implied by tables/figures

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Word embedding via parameterized encoding circuits
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Classification metrics computed from measurement outcomes

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: Loss curves shown; QNN-SAMo converges faster than QNN-SAMb

speedup_claims.caveats: No speedup claim; only empirical classification improvements and parameter efficiency are reported.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: 8 qubits, 88 gate depth for QNN-SAMb; 8/72 for QNN-SAMo; no hardware execution reported
limiting_factors: No QPU hardware or runtime evidence
Performance is comparable to or only modestly better than classical SAM on RP
No asymptotic speedup or crossover analysis
Word embedding and circuit preparation overhead are substantial

notes: Hardware platform is not named; no simulator or QPU is specified.
The paper reports qubit counts and gate depths for the text tasks in Table 3 (e.g., complexity 8/88 and 8/72), but not a single universal depth across all variants.
No asymptotic speedup analysis is provided; only empirical comparisons against classical SAM and prior quantum baselines.
On MC, QNN-SAM and SAM both achieve 100% accuracy.
On RP, QNN-SAMo reaches 74.19% accuracy versus 67.74% for SAM, but this is still a small benchmark and not a practical advantage claim.

experiments.description: QNN-SAMo and QNN-SAMb evaluated on stock closing-price prediction for 12 public stocks using four-day historical windows.

algorithm.variant: QNN-SAMo / QNN-SAMb for stock price prediction
algorithm.ansatz: U1, U2, U3 parameterized quantum circuits; U2 uses controlled phase gates and Rx-Rz rotation gates; U3 uses CRX-based two-qubit blocks
algorithm.parameter_initialization: random initialization of parameters (five repetitions with random initialization)

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Each of the four preceding days is encoded with a single Rx rotation gate; n1=1 for the encoding circuit
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize mean squared error for next-day closing price prediction

problem_instance.description: Predict next-day closing price from the previous four days of six stock indices

dataset_specification.description: Tickers: AAPL, AMGN, BA, CAT, CSCO, HD, IBM, JNJ, JPM, KO, MMM, MSFT; 1259 trading days per stock; 6 indices per day; normalized to [0,1] using min-max scaling

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Reported R2, RMSE, and MAPE for each stock; comparison across QNN-SAMo, QNN-SAMb, and SAM

implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: R2, RMSE, and MAPE computed from predicted vs true closing prices

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: Loss curves shown; QNN-SAMo generally converges faster than QNN-SAMb

speedup_claims.caveats: No speedup claim; the paper reports better forecasting metrics than SAM on most stocks.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: 8 qubits, 96 gate depth, 72 two-qubit gates; no hardware execution reported
limiting_factors: No QPU hardware or runtime evidence
Classical SAM is close in performance and sometimes better on individual stocks/metrics
No asymptotic complexity or crossover analysis
Financial time-series loading and variational optimization overhead remain unresolved

notes: Hardware platform is not specified in the paper.
The paper reports qubit counts and gate depths for the stock task in Table 5 (QNN-SAMo 8 qubits, depth 96; QNN-SAMb 8 qubits, depth 112).
No asymptotic speedup claim is made; the paper reports empirical forecasting metrics only.
QNN-SAMo generally improves R2 and RMSE/MAPE over SAM, but the paper does not establish a practical quantum advantage.

experiments.description: Robustness study of QNN-SAMo under common quantum noise channels on the meteorological, text, and stock tasks.

algorithm.variant: QNN-SAMo robustness under noisy quantum circuits
algorithm.ansatz: Same QNN-SAMo circuit as in the main experiments; noise applied to the U3 layer

hyperparameters.loss_function: task-dependent (MSE for regression, binary cross-entropy for classification)

algorithm.parameter_initialization: random initialization of parameters (five repetitions with random initialization)

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Same as the corresponding clean-task encodings; noise injected after circuit construction
problem_formulation.objective_function: Assess robustness of prediction/classification accuracy under noise

problem_instance.description: Noise robustness evaluation on meteorological indicators, MC text classification, and RP text classification

dataset_specification.description: Same datasets and splits as the clean experiments

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Same preprocessing as the clean experiments
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Accuracy measured under each noise channel and noise level; mean and standard deviation over five repetitions

noise_model.noise_type: bit-flip, depolarizing, amplitude damping, phase flip, phase damping
noise_model.error_mitigation_method: none reported; discussion mentions ZNE and randomized compilation as possible mitigations, but not used in the reported experiments

speedup_claims.caveats: Noise robustness is evaluated empirically; no speedup claim is made.

notes: This is a noise-injection study on the same gate-based QNN-SAMo circuits; the paper does not name a simulator or QPU, so simulator_noisy is inferred from the Kraus-operator noise modeling.
The paper explicitly states that noise is applied to the eight qubits of the U3 layer.
No asymptotic speedup analysis is provided.

experiments.description: Robustness evaluation of QNN-SAMo under five quantum noise channels on the meteorological, MC, and RP tasks.

algorithm.ansatz: Same QNN-SAMo PQC architecture with noise applied to the U3 layer

key_results: Noise channels: bit-flip, depolarizing, amplitude damping, phase flip, phase damping.
Table 6 reports that MC remains at 100% accuracy across all listed noise levels.
RP accuracy drops from 74.19% without noise to 58.99% under amplitude damping at p=0.05, and to 60.61% under bit-flip at p=0.01.
Meteorological tasks remain near 99.8%-93.5% accuracy for low noise levels.

experiments.description: Scaling study of QNN-SAMo on four meteorological forecasting horizons with sequence lengths 2, 3, 4, and 5.

algorithm.ansatz: Same QNN-SAMo PQC architecture with varying U2/U3 sizes

key_results: Table 7 reports qubit counts 4, 6, 8, and 10 for sequence lengths 2, 3, 4, and 5.
Mean accuracies remain high: atmospheric pressure 99.85%-99.87%, temperature 93.35%-93.51%, relative humidity 90.43%-92.54%.
